purpose: Locate the Hunyuan3D-Paint 2.1 VRAM peak and measure studio-runner release_stages; calibration only, not texture candidates.
findings: Resident paint fills the 24 GiB card at every setting; nvidia-smi read 23.85-23.90 GiB used for 6x512, 6x768, 9x768 and 12x768.
Model weights hold 7.7 GiB. Diffusion steps add about 1.6 GiB. The peak is the VAE decode of all albedo and metal-rough views in one batch at the end of multiview generation.
At 12 views x 768 the torch reserved pool reached 35.5 GiB, so about 11 GiB spilled into Windows shared memory.
Paint is deterministic: two resident runs gave byte-identical maps at 6x512 and 12x768. Released runs are deterministic too (launcher rerun byte-identical).

Offloading the diffusion weights alone kept maps byte-identical but did not lower the peak. Decode-one-at-a-time slicing lowers it and is not byte-identical; slicing the reference encode as well moved more pixels, so only the decode is sliced.

floors_mib.basis: released peak reserved (11.8 / 16.1 GiB) plus about 2.5 GiB for the CUDA context and headroom; unmeasured combinations take the 12x768 floor
